=== About Mr. Inabe ===

This Harusumi Takako (later renamed Akiko) was the eldest daughter of {{ill|Council|qid=Council|lt=Council}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Daisuke Shikibu}}{{ill|Yoshitada Haruzumi|ja|春澄善縄|qid=Q11513769}}, and {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|qid=Q349243|lt=Seiwa}} , {{ill|Emperor Yōzei|Q349280|qid=Q349280|lt=Yosei}}, {{ill|Emperor Kōkō|Q440518|qid=Q440518|lt=Mitsuko}}, {{ill|Emperor Uda|Q349267|qid=Q349267|lt=Uda}}, and {{ill|Emperor Daigo|Q329753|qid=Q329753|lt=Daigo}}. It is said that he especially had the trust of Emperor Uda.Zenna was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Zou Inabe}}, and his grandfather {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inabezaimaro}} was {{ill|Ise Province|be|Ісэ (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئیسێ|cs|Provincie Ise|de|Provinz Ise|es|Provincia de Ise|eu|Ise probintzia|fa|ولایت ایسه|fi|Isen provinssi|fr|Province d'Ise|gl|Provincia de Ise|hak|Yî-sṳ-koet|id|Provinsi Ise|it|Ise (provincia)|ja|伊勢国|ko|이세국|lt|Isės žemė|nl|Ise (provincie)|pt|Província de Ise|ru|Исэ (провинция)|simple|Ise Province|sk|Ise (provincia)|sr|Провинција Исе|tr|Ise (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ісе|zh|伊勢國|zh_min_nan|Ise-kok|zh_yue|伊勢國|qid=Q864166}}{{ill|Inabe District|ceb|Inabe-gun|ckb|گەڕەکی ئینابێ|es|Distrito de Inabe|fa|شهرستان اینابه، میه|fr|District d'Inabe|id|Distrik Inabe, Mie|it|Distretto di Inabe|ja|員弁郡|ko|이나베군|pl|Powiat Inabe|uk|Повіт Інабе|zh|員辨郡|qid=Q1131499}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=small territory}}, his father {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyoo Inabe}} was {{ill|Suō Province|Q1053037|qid=Q1053037}} large {{jalink|eyes}. (Kokushi)|Q11581532|He was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Junior Eighth Lower}}, the lowest rank among government officials. Zenkyu was intelligent and hardworking at a young age and rose through the ranks, and in {{ill|Tenchō|de|Tenchō|es|Tenchō|fa|تنچو|fr|Ère Tenchō|ia|Tencho|id|Tenchō|ja|天長|ko|덴초|ru|Тэнтё|simple|Tenchō|sr|Тенчо|th|เท็นโจ|tr|Tenchō|uk|Тентьо|zh|天長 (日本)|zh_yue|天長 (年號)|qid=Q1373138}} 5th year ({{ill|828|Q30375|qid=Q30375}}), Zenkyu and his five brothers and sisters were given the surname of Harusumi Sukune. (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōkan}} In February 12 ({{ill|870|Q23629|qid=Q23629}}), Harusumi Zenkyusaden</ref>, in addition to Takako, a female Zenkyoku, was given to the priests, as well as a man who had a strong attitude toward men (Junior Fifth Rank Upper {{ill|Kuzen-cho|Q11650312|qid=Q11650312|lt=Kuzen-cho}} Kanesuo no kami, Gusei), {{ill|Uosui|Q79843706|qid=Q79843706|lt=Uosui}} ({{ill|Nuidonokami|Q11608161|qid=Q11608161|lt=Nuidonokami}} Junior Fifth Rank Lower). Zennawa served during the three dynasties of {{ill|Emperor Ninmyō|Q349271|qid=Q349271|lt=Ninmyo}}, {{ill|Emperor Montoku|Q357225|qid=Q357225|lt=Buntoku}}, and {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|qid=Q349243|lt=Along with Yoshio}} and {{ill|Yasuno no Toyomichi|Q17221777|qid=Q17221777}}, he wrote {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}, the fourth of the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168}}, and is referred to as ``Confucianism in the Dynasty'' in the "Fuso Ryakki". In the end, he died in the 12th year of Jogan ({{ill|870|Q23629|qid=Q23629}}) while serving concurrently as the councilor of {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|ko|종3위|zh|從三位|qid=Q11071123}}, Daisuke Shikibu, and the governor of Sanuki. Takako dedicated it to Inabe Shrine three years after her father's death.There are various theories about the origin of the Inabe clan. In the August 31st year of the Ojin era in the Nihon Shoki, the king of Silla presented his excellent craftsmanship to the Kingdom of Wa as atonement for the 500 imperial court ships that were being built and moored at Muko Sluice (Muko Minato) when a fire broke out in the Silla envoy's ship and the imperial court ships were completely burnt down. It is said that this family of craftsmen was the ancestors of Inabe. Tradition and duties of Inabe]</ref>. However, in the "Shinsei Shojiroku", it is written that the enshrined deity {{ill|Ikagashiko-o|fr|Ikagashikoo|ja|伊香色雄|qid=Q55536799|lt=Ikagashikio-no-Mikoto}} is the ancestral god of the Inabe clan, the older brother of the Tenson {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Keijoki-no-Mikoto}}, and the sixth-generation grandson of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Narahayahi-no-Mikoto}}. In "{{ill|Kujiki|Q2716751|qid=Q2716751}}" {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenjin Honki}}, it is said that five people offered offerings to Rokuhaya Hime when he descended from heaven. This is called “Gobujin” (Itsutomononokami), and they are
* Amatsumara - the founder of {{ill|Mononobe officials|Q55521285|qid=Q55521285}}
* Amatsuyuso - Founder of {{ill|Kasanuimura|Q11599947|qid=Q11599947|lt=Kasanuibu}} etc.
* Amatsu Akaura
* Hohoro - {{ill|Toichi district|Q11405036|qid=Q11405036|lt=Toichibe}}The ancestor of the heads* Amatsu Akaboshi - Tsukushi {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Genda}} Father of Mononobe et al.
Of these, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsu Akaboshi}} or {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsu Akaboshi}} is said to be the ancestor of the Inabe clan.

Osaka|zh|池田市|zh_classical|池田市|zh_min_nan|Ikeda-chhī|zh_yue|池田|qid=Q817965}}) was once the site of {{ill|Ina no Agata|Q11571881|qid=Q11571881}} during the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|Q2658252|qid=Q2658252}} era, and Tamenatsuhiko<ref>{{ill|Inatsuhiko Shrine|Q11567184|qid=Q11567184}} History. It is said to have been ruled by a family headed by </ref>. However, the genealogy from here to Inbenzaimaro and Toyo is not clear.

In {{ill|Wadō (era)|Q1373026|qid=Q1373026}}6 ({{ill|713|Q23523|qid=Q23523}}), by the imperial order of the 43rd {{ill|Empress Genmei|Q233224|qid=Q233224}}, the family name of Inabe was changed to 'Inabe'.Although there are no historical materials that directly link this Inabe to his origin, it is said that he had the skill of a craftsman in woodworking architecture, and in August 17th year ({{ill|745|Q23612|qid=Q23612}}), the 45th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|qid=Q349263}}, established the Inabe family. For the construction of {{ill|Tōdai-ji|Q460367|qid=Q460367}}, {{ill|Inabe no Momoyo|Q55536849|qid=Q55536849}} from the Inabe clan was mobilized as a carpenter (=master carpenter), and {{ill|Masuda no Nawate|Q66364942|qid=Q66364942}}, a master craftsman from Hida, was mobilized as a carpenter (=deputy master carpenter). Furthermore, there are records that he was involved in the construction of {{ill|Hōryū-ji|Q261932|qid=Q261932}}, {{ill|Ishiyama-dera|Q1082791|qid=Q1082791}}, and {{ill|Kōfuku-ji|Q1070863|qid=Q1070863}}, and from artifacts excavated from ancient tombs, it is known that he was also involved in the construction of {{ill|Asuka-dera|Q779755|qid=Q779755}}.

=== Reitaisai ===

=== Taisha (Oyashiro) Festival ===
The first weekend of April every year (excluding the first day of the month) - Although it is not classified as a major shrine, it has been called the Taisha Festival since its inception.

=== Ageuma Shinto ritual ===
Shiraku Festival, Honraku Festival, intangible folk cultural assets of Mie Prefecture from {{ill|2002|Q1987|qid=Q1987}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}14). Run on a 100m horse track and run up a 2.5m high {{ill|Earthworks (archaeology)|Q1349587|qid=Q1349587}}<ref name="cn1604"/>. <ref name="cn1604"/> is a Shinto ritual to predict fortunes and fortunes. Riders in their late teens chosen from each of the four local regions spend a certain period of time {{ill|Misogi|Q1936265|qid=Q1936265}} in advance, and each race up the earthworks with their horses twice on the first day of the festival and once on the second day, and those who succeed sing kachidoki chants in the precincts.

{{ill|Kenkyū|Q1193933|qid=Q1193933}} December 3rd year ({{ill|1192|Q19739|qid=Q19739}}), {{ill|Oki Castle|Q105260558|qid=Q105260558}} Lord {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gunji}} It is said that {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inben Saburo Yukitsuna}} started it in Oinohara in order to improve the morale of young people after {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}} informed him of his desire for horse shooting and maki-gari. It dates back about 160 years to the Ageuma Shinto ritual at {{ill|Tado Taisha|Q116140|qid=Q116140}} in the prefecture.It took its current form in {{ill|Kennin|Q1195433|qid=Q1195433}}3 ({{ill|1203|Q5227|qid=Q5227}}), when it was falsely accused that Yukitsuna had assassinated the shugo of {{ill|Ise Province|be|Ісэ (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئیسێ|cs|Provincie Ise|de|Provinz Ise|es|Provincia de Ise|eu|Ise probintzia|fa|ولایت ایسه|fi|Isen provinssi|fr|Province d'Ise|gl|Provincia de Ise|hak|Yî-sṳ-koet|id|Provinsi Ise|it|Ise (provincia)|ja|伊勢国|ko|이세국|lt|Isės žemė|nl|Ise (provincie)|pt|Província de Ise|ru|Исэ (провинция)|simple|Ise Province|sk|Ise (provincia)|sr|Провинција Исе|tr|Ise (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ісе|zh|伊勢國|zh_min_nan|Ise-kok|zh_yue|伊勢國|qid=Q864166}}. It is said that this was the work of the remnants of the Taira clan, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Wakana Goro Moritaka}}, who dedicates land in a corner of the precincts of Inabe Shrine for divine protection, built an ``age slope'' and dedicated raised horses and yabusame.Since {{ill|2020|Q25337|qid=Q25337}} (Reiwa 2), {{ill|socio-economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in Japan|Q86732769|qid=Q86732769|lt=New coronavirus The situation continues to be canceled due to measures to prevent the spread of infectious diseases}}, and in {{ill|2023|Q49622|qid=Q49622}} (Reiwa 5), only the ``Umahiki'' parade, in which people ride horses around the shrine grounds, will be held.<ref>{{Cite news |Japanese book |title="Ageba/Yasubime" held again this year at Toin's Inabe Shrine Taisha Festival |newspaper={{ill|Chunichi Shimbun|Q904678|qid=Q904678}} |date=2023-04-10 |url=https://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/669340 |access-date=2023-12-07}}</ref>, Even after {{ill|2024|Q49619|qid=Q49619|lt=next year}}, only "Umahiki" will be held because "the number of people in the area who keep horses has decreased due to the coronavirus pandemic, and the know-how of Shinto rituals cannot be passed on."<ref name = "NHK2023-12-04">{{Cite news |Japanese book |title=Toin Town "Ageuma Shinto" ritual is not held; it is difficult to pass on the know-how due to the coronavirus |newspaper={{ill|NHK Tsu Broadcasting Station|Q10854723|qid=Q10854723|lt=NHK Mie}} {{ill|NHK News|Q10851844|qid=Q10851844|lt=NEWS WEB}} |date=2023-12-04 |url=https://www3.nhk.or.jp/lnews/tsu/20231204/3070011826.html |access-date=2023-12-07}}</ref>.

==== Criticism ====As {{ill|Animal welfare|Q459426|qid=Q459426|lt=animal welfare awareness}} has increased in recent years, there has been criticism that it is {{ill|Cruelty to animals|Q40053|qid=Q40053|lt=abuse}}. |publisher={{ill|Animal Rights Center Japan|Q17191587|qid=Q17191587}} |date=2017-07-01 |accessdate=2023-05-12}}</ref> (Also refer to "{{ill|Tado Festival|Q116021|qid=Q116021}}"), a prefectural investigation found that in {{ill|2010|Q1995|qid=Q1995}} (2010), one horse died on the spot after falling, {{ill|2011|Q1994|qid=Q1994|lt=the following year}} and {{ill|2015|Q2002|qid=Q2002}} (2015), one animal was found to have been {{ill|Animal euthanasia|Q652653|qid=Q652653}} by a {{ill|Veterinarian|Q202883|qid=Q202883|lt=veterinarian}} after suffering a broken bone.<ref>{{Cite news |Japanese book |title=Toin-cho Inabe Shrine's "age horse ritual" 3 horses die in 11 years |newspaper=NHK Mie NEWS WEB |date=2023-07-04 |url=https://www3.nhk.or.jp/lnews/tsu/20230704/3070010808.html |access-date=2023-11-03}}</ref>.Due to this, critical opinions have been received at Inabe Shrine and Toin Town Hall<ref name = "NHK2023-12-04" {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=As mentioned above}}, from 2023 onwards, only "Umahiki" will be held, and {{ill|Aya Sugimoto|Q442667|qid=Q442667}}, who has criticized the Ageuma Shinto ritual as an animal rights activist, calls it a "wise decision". Abolitionism is strong on the internet: Aya Sugimoto says, ``What should we do about Tado Taisha Shrine?'' |newspaper={{ill|Chunichi Sports|Q11365074|qid=Q11365074}} |date=2023-12-06 |url=https://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/818091 |access-date=2023-12-07}}</ref>.
